Mylona z trującymi, białymi muchomorami,: Confused with poisonous white amanitas ('muchomor' (Polish name)), e.g. the venomous one. Unlike them it has no bulb or volva at the stem base and no whitish gills; in champignons the gills are pink, reddish-brown, up to brown-black.
Blaszki różowoszare. Trzon białawy o cie: Gills pinkish-grey. Stem whitish with a thin and delicate ring, bulbously widened at the base. Flesh white, turning chrome yellow when cut at the stem base. Smell unpleasant, of carbolic acid (especially when boiling or frying). Poisonous!
Kapelusz […] brązowawy z białymi plamkam: Cap […] brownish with white spots that rain may wash off. Stem cylindrical, slender, smooth, with a hanging smooth ring and a volva in the form of rolls, on a bulbous base. Smell of radish. Strongly poisonous! Sometimes confused with 'czubajka kania' (Polish name).
Kapelusz […] zielonawy (niekiedy biały),: Cap […] greenish (sometimes white), shiny. Stem with a zigzag pattern, with a hanging ring, cylindrical with a bulbously thickened base and a white, sac-like, torn volva. Smell bland, sweetish. Deadly poisonous! Confused with 'gaska zielonka' (Polish name), 'golabek zielonawy' (Polish name) and champignons.
Kapelusz […] pokryty nieregularnymi szar: Cap […] covered with irregular grey-violet patches. Gills white and crowded. Stem […] with a thickened bulbous base, with a ring. […] Inedible, weakly poisonous! Confused with 'gaska nieksztaltna' (Polish name) and 'muchomor czerwonawy' (Polish name).
Blaszki białe, przy brzegu kapelusza zao: Gills white, rounded at the cap margin. Stem slender, cylindrical, white and smooth with a bulbous base surrounded by a white, spreading and torn volva. Ring white, thin and not very large. […] Deadly poisonous! Confused with young champignons and 'majowka wiosenna' (Polish name).
Kapelusz dzwonkowaty, potem bardziej pła: Cap bell-shaped, then flatter, whitish with a striate margin. Stem cylindrical, scaly-fibrous with a bulbously thickened base and a membranous volva; ring vestigial or absent. Smell of radish. Deadly poisonous! Young fruiting bodies are confused with champignons.
Kapelusz […] beżowy lub brązowy z drobny: Cap […] beige or brown with small, dark scales. Stem cylindrical and curved with a thickened base, yellowish-brown, bast-fibrous with a distinct ring. […] Only the caps are edible. Undercooked it may be harmful. Confused with 'maslanka wiazkowa' (Polish name) ('lysiczka trujaca' (Polish name)).
Spód kapelusza zbudowany z rurek, któryc: The underside of the cap is made of tubes whose openings (pores) are at first whitish, cream, later yellow-green, and do not change colour when touched. Stem solid, barrel-shaped, later club-shaped, whitish, light brown with a fine net of veins […] Confused with 'goryczak zolciowy' (Polish name) and 'borowik szatanski' (Polish name).
Spód żółtocytrynowy, żółtooliwkowy, po d: Underside lemon yellow, yellow-olive, turns blue when touched. Stem thick, strong, solid and club-shaped, yellow at the top, red in the middle and brown-red at the bottom, with a distinct net everywhere. […] Taste at first mild, then bitter. Poisonous! Confused with 'borowik ceglastopory' (Polish name).
Od kwietnia do czerwca […] Blaszki biała: From April to June […] Gills whitish to cream, crowded and thin, narrow, notched at the stem. […] Flesh firm, whitish, with a mealy taste and smell. Edible. Confused with 'wieruszka zatokowata' (Polish name), 'strzepiak ceglasty' (Polish name) and white amanitas ('muchomor' (Polish name)).
Owocnik wypukły, potem lejkowaty z niere: Fruiting body convex, then funnel-shaped with an irregular margin, yellow. Stem of the same colour, widened at the top, solid. Ridge-like gills run down the stem. The taste of the raw fruiting body is acrid, peppery. Confused with the inedible 'lisowka pomaranczowa' (Polish name), the so-called false chanterelle.
Blaszki żółtawe, potem brązowe, gęste, z: Gills yellowish, then brown, crowded, with a notched edge. Stem white, yellowish, cylindrical, thickened at the base, longitudinally striate, solid, with a narrow membranous ring that disappears with time. […] Confused with 'strzepiak ceglasty' (Polish name).
Blaszki białawe, potem różowawe, przy tr: Gills whitish, then pinkish, sinuately notched at the stem. Stem whitish or light yellow […] without a ring. Flesh white, shiny, with a floury taste and smell. Strongly poisonous! Confused with 'gesnica (majowka) wiosenna' (Polish name) and champignons.
[…] na rozkładającym się drewnie iglasty: […] on decaying coniferous wood, less often deciduous. […] Stem […] with a skin-like, short-lived, whitish or brown ring, below which it is whitish-fibrillose. Flesh brownish, thin, with a floury taste and smell. Deadly poisonous! Confused with 'luszczak zmienny' (Polish name).
Główka nieregularnie kulista i pofałdowa: Head irregularly spherical and folded, hollow inside, chestnut or dark brown. Stem short, cylindrical, whitish. Flesh brittle and waxy. Pleasant smell. Deadly poisonous! Confused with 'smardz' (Polish name).
Kapelusz wypukły, potem lejkowaty o podw: Cap convex, then funnel-shaped with inrolled margins, orange or brownish, matt, elastic. Gills intensely orange. Stem thin, slender, widened upwards, smooth. Inedible! Confused with 'pieprznik jadalny' (Polish name), that is the chanterelle ('kurka' (Polish name)).
Kapelusz […] żółty lub rdzawobrązowy, z: Cap […] yellow or rusty brown, with a darker centre, smooth and shiny. Stem cylindrical, slender, bent and hollow, covered with fibres. Flesh with an unpleasant smell. The whole bunch is fused at the base. Poisonous! Confused with honey fungi ('opienki' (Polish name)).
Kapelusz […] promieniście popękany […] B: Cap […] radially cracked […] Gills whitish, then brownish, crowded, turning red when damaged. […] Flesh fleshy, turning red when cut, with a sweetish, fruity smell and a mild taste. Deadly poisonous (contains a lot of muscarine)! Confused with 'plachetka zwyczajna' (Polish name) and 'gesnica (majowka) wiosenna' (Polish name).
Preferuje drewno drzew liściastych, rzad: Prefers the wood of deciduous trees, less often coniferous. […] The stem below the disappearing ring is covered with brown scales. […] Edible (woody stems should be cut off). Confused with the poisonous 'helmowka obrzezona' (Polish name).
Od sierpnia do listopada pojedynczo lub: From August to November singly or in groups under pines. […] Gills orange, turn green when crushed. Stem cylindrical with dark spots. Orange milk in the flesh. […] It is sometimes confused with the poisonous ones: 'mleczaj welnianka' (Polish name) and 'krowiak podwiniety' (Polish name).
[…] wyłącznie pod brzozami. Kapelusz […]: […] exclusively under birches. Cap […] with an inrolled margin, orange to light brown with dark concentric rings, hairy. […] Exudes abundant white milk that tastes burning. Poisonous! Confused with 'rydz' (Polish name).
Przypomina odwróconą pękatą butelkę lub: Resembles an inverted plump bottle or a pear. The white fruiting body is covered with spines. Inside also white and compact, later it darkens and takes on a musty smell. Edible as long as its interior is white and elastic. It is sometimes confused with the poisonous 'tegoskor cytrynowy' (Polish name).
Kapelusz […] z małym garbem na szczycie,: Cap […] with a small hump at the top, dry, cracked, covered with spreading scales, in various shades of brown. Stem long, slender, bulbous at the base, in the upper part with a double, movable ring, hollow inside. […] Only the cap is edible. Sometimes confused with the spotted amanita ('muchomor plamisty' (Polish name)).
Kapelusz półkolisty, stożkowaty, potem p: Cap semicircular, conical, then flat, with a darker hump, flesh-coloured, light brown, darker when wet, smooth. Gills of a similar colour, fairly thick and widely spaced. […] Edible (only the caps are used). Confused with the poisonous 'lejkowka lisciowa' (Polish name).
Na kapeluszu barwy od szarej do brązowoż: On the cap, coloured from grey to brownish-yellow, there are characteristic folds and pits surrounded by ribs – like a honeycomb. Under partial species protection outside gardens, horticultural crops, forest nurseries and green areas. Confused with the poisonous 'piestrzenica kasztanowata' (Polish name).
Spód żółtawooliwkowy, potem ceglastoczer: Underside yellowish-olive, then brick-red, turns blue when pressed. Stem yellowish with red tufts or grains, without a net […] Flesh yellow, turning blue when cut, with a mild taste and smell. Edible. Confused with the poisonous 'borowik grubotrzonowy' (Polish name).
Kapelusz wypukły, potem płaski i lejkowa: Cap convex, then flat and funnel-shaped with an inrolled margin, velvety, brown Stem short, cylindrical, stocky, narrowed at the base. Formerly considered edible. Poisonous! It is sometimes confused with 'mleczaj rudy' (Polish name) and with 'rydz' (Polish name) – unlike it, it does not exude milk.
Kapelusz wypukły, potem płaski i w końcu: Cap convex, then flat and finally depressed, reddish, sticky during rain. Stem cylindrical, smooth and brittle, mostly pure white. Smell fruity. Confused with 'golabek wyborny' (Polish name) (edible). Unlike it, 'golabek wymiotny' (Polish name) has a sharp and burning taste.
Kapelusz […] czerwonawy, cielistoróżowy,: Cap […] reddish, flesh-pink, in places discoloured to an ochre colour. Skin sticky during rain, often does not reach the margin of the cap. Stem cylindrical, solid, whitish. […] It is sometimes confused with the poisonous 'golabek wymiotny' (Polish name), which has a burning taste.
Kapelusz kulisty, potem rozpostarty z wg: Cap spherical, then spread out with a depression in the middle, grey-green, green-blue or olive. Initially smooth, quickly cracked in a characteristic pattern of small blocks. Confused with the deadly poisonous 'muchomor zielonawy' (Polish name) ('sromotnikowy' (Polish name)).
Owocnik kulisty lub bulwiasty, przypomin: Fruiting body spherical or tuberous, resembles a potato, yellowish or brown, without a stem, covered with protruding scales. The interior of the fruiting body is white and hard, then black, resembling ground poppy seed. Smell strong, spicy. Poisonous! It may be confused with 'purchawka chropowata' (Polish name).
Gills bright yellow, thin and brittle. […] Flesh hard, fleshy, whitish, with a mild taste. Edible. However, it may cause dangerous poisoning if larger amounts are eaten regularly. Confused with 'gaska siarkowa' (Polish name) and even the death cap ('muchomor sromotnikowy' (Polish name)).
Kapelusz płaski z garbkiem pośrodku, sza: Cap flat with a hump in the centre, greyish with a violet-brown tinge, smooth, with black radial fibres. Stem whitish, cylindrical, solid, in old age, like the gills, with a yellow-green sheen. Confused with poisonous amanitas ('muchomor' (Polish name)), e.g. the porfirowy one ('muchomor porfirowy' (Polish name)).
Blaszki żółte, dość rzadkie i grube. […]: Gills yellow, rather distant and thick. […] Flesh sulphur-yellow, thin and fibrous, with an unpleasant taste and a suffocating smell of carbide. Inedible, weakly poisonous. Confused with 'gaska zielonka' (Polish name).
Rurki i pory białawe, z wiekiem lub po d: Tubes and pores whitish, with age or when touched they change colour to pink to pink-brown. Stem […] with a distinct brownish net. Flesh white, very bitter, but with a pleasant smell. Inedible! Causes severe gastrointestinal disorders. Confused with 'borowik szlachetny' (Polish name).
Kapelusz borowika […] Rurki u młodych os: The cap of the 'borowik' (Polish name) […] The tubes in young specimens are almost white, in older ones yellow-olive. Stem thick, barrel-shaped, sand-coloured with a whitish net of veins. The inedible 'goryczak zolciowy' (Polish name) is characterised by a stem with a brown net with long meshes and a pink-coloured tube layer. In young specimens the tubes are dirty white. Cap cushion-shaped, suede-like. Even a small addition of 'goryczak' (Polish name) to a dish prepared from 'borowiki' (Polish name) will make it unfit to eat because of the strong bitterness.
Cechą rozpoznawczą czubajki kani jest zy: The distinguishing features of the 'czubajka kania' (Polish name) are the zigzag pattern on the stem, the movable ring, the cap with a hump, the white, unchanging flesh, the bulbous base without a volva. A 'czubajka' (Polish name) that causes poisoning, such as the 'czubajka czerwieniejaca' (Polish name), can be told apart by the distinct, protruding scales on the cap, the red colouring of the gills and stem after damage, and the absence of a darker pattern on the stem. In turn, the poisonous 'czubajka ostroluskowa' (Polish name) has a cap covered with conical scales, a non-sliding ring and an unpleasant smell. A mistake between the 'czubajka kania' (Polish name) and the 'muchomor zielonawy' (Polish name) is a deadly danger. It has a greenish, smooth (without patches) cap without a hump, an immovable ring and a bulb with a volva. In turn, the 'muchomor plamisty' (Polish name) is distinguished from the 'kania' (Polish name) by lighter, white patches on a brown cap that has no hump, a hanging ring and a bulb at the base of the stem.
Czubajka kania, czubajka czerwieniejąca,: 'Czubajka kania' (Polish name), 'czubajka czerwieniejaca' (Polish name), 'ostroluskowa' (Polish name), and the deadly poisonous amanitas
Gąskę zielonkę możemy pomylić z gąską si: We may confuse the 'gaska zielonka' (Polish name) with the 'gaska siarkowa' (Polish name), which is poisonous when raw, and when cooked – inedible because of the unpleasant smell of carbide. Other characteristic features of the edible 'gaska' (Polish name) are yellow, densely arranged gills, a smell of flour and whitish flesh.
Trzon pusty z brązowym pierścieniem, pon: Stem hollow with a brown ring, scaly below it, bald in older ones. The 'luszczak zmienny' (Polish name) has a pleasant mushroom smell and grows on the wood of deciduous trees. We may confuse it with the deadly poisonous 'helmowka jadowita' (Polish name), which gives off a smell of flour, grows on the wood of coniferous trees, and has a white ring below which the stem has a structure with white fibrils.
Łuszczak zmienny, a śmiertelnie trująca: 'Luszczak zmienny' (Polish name) and the deadly poisonous 'helmowka jadowita' (Polish name)
Mleczaj rydz ma pomarańczowe blaszki, kt: The 'mleczaj rydz' (Polish name) has orange gills that turn green when damaged but never turn wine-red. The milk is carrot-coloured; as it dries it fades and turns grey-green, but never discolours to wine-red. It is also worth remembering that the 'mleczaj rydz' (Polish name) grows only under pines. A particular health hazard is a mistake with the 'mleczaj welnianka' (Polish name). Its gills are white, the milk burning and white. The fringed-tufted margin of the cap is characteristic. It grows only under birches. The toxic 'krowiak podwiniety' (Polish name), called 'olszowka' (Polish name), should also be avoided. This mushroom does not exude milk when damaged. Instead, the gills and stem turn red-brown.
Mleczaj rydz, a trujący mleczaj wełniank: 'Mleczaj rydz' (Polish name) and the poisonous 'mleczaj welnianka' (Polish name) and 'krowiak podwiniety' (Polish name)
Muchomor zielonawy jest jednym z najsiln: The 'muchomor zielonawy' (Polish name) is one of the most strongly poisonous mushrooms. The characteristic features of this mushroom are: always white, cream gills; a smooth cap surface; a hanging, non-sliding ring on the stem, under the cap; a thick bulb surrounded by a volva; a sweet smell resembling artificial honey. […] The 'czubajka kania' (Polish name) is distinguished by scales on the cap, a movable ring and a bulb without a volva. If during mushroom picking we are guided solely by the colour of the cap, a mistake may concern the 'golabek zielonawy' (Polish name). However, the 'golabek' (Polish name) has neither a ring nor a volva, the stem is smooth, and the surface of the cap in adult specimens is characteristically cracked into patches. When collecting young specimens, the poisonous amanita may also be confused with the 'gaska zielonka' (Polish name). Here the characteristic features distinguishing the 'gaska' (Polish name) are yellow gills, no ring and no volva, and a decidedly smaller size of adult specimens. […] collect only adult fruiting bodies that have already developed their characteristic features.
Śmiertelnie trujący muchomor zielonawy,: The deadly poisonous 'muchomor zielonawy' (Polish name) and similar edible species
Opieńka miodowa jest jadalnym grzybem, j: The 'opienka miodowa' (Polish name) is an edible mushroom, but only young caps are fit for consumption. We may confuse the 'opienka miodowa' (Polish name) with the 'maslanka wiazkowa' (Polish name). Both grow in dense groups on stumps, but the 'maslanka' (Polish name) is decidedly distinguished by a smooth cap, no ring and a very bitter taste.
Do pomyłki może dojść przy ocenie młodyc: A mistake may occur when assessing young fruiting bodies. Therefore let us remember to collect champignons when they have developed their distinguishing features. The most important feature is the gills of champignons. The edible ones are at first pale grey, then pink, and finally blackish. The poisonous 'pieczarka karbolowa' (Polish name) greatly resembles the edible champignon. In this case the 'pieczarka karbolowa' (Polish name) is decidedly distinguished by its smell and its reaction to damage. If it turns yellow after damage and at the same time smells unpleasant, we are dealing with the 'pieczarka karbolowa' (Polish name). If we want to make additionally sure, we can cut the champignon and place it in a bowl of hot water – the smell of carbolic acid will be more intense. The characteristic feature that distinguishes the 'muchomor jadowity' (Polish name) from edible champignons is the invariably white, or possibly slightly cream, gills throughout the life of this mushroom.
Pieczarki jadalne, pieczarka trująca (ka: Edible champignons, the poisonous (carbolic) 'pieczarka' (Polish name), and the deadly poisonous amanitas
Fałszywa kurka będzie miała kapelusz, bl: The false chanterelle will have the cap, gills and stem in the same orange colour. Elastic, soft and orange flesh. Stem decidedly narrower than that of the edible chanterelle […] The 'pieprznik jadalny' (Polish name) can be recognised by the stem slightly lighter than the cap and the white flesh.
Smardz pojawia się w lasach już w kwietn: The 'smardz' (Polish name) appears in forests as early as April. It is distinguished by a fruiting body that is almost round or slightly elongated with wide pits. It is hollow throughout the cross-section. In turn, the 'piestrzenica kasztanowata' (Polish name) has an irregularly folded surface resembling a brain, and its cap is fused with the stem.
